mathematics.question: Convert 101101 base two to a number in base ten.
Convert 47 in base ten to binary (base two).
Express 342 base five as a base-ten number.
Simplify x⁵ ÷ x².
mathematics.explanation: When dividing powers of the same base, subtract the indices: x⁵⁻² = x³.

mathematics.question: Evaluate log₂ 32.
In a class of 40 students, 25 play football and 18 play basketball. If 8 play both games, how many play neither?
Expand and simplify (2x + 3)(x − 4).
Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm. (Take π = 22/7)
A right-angled triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
Find the roots of the equation x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
What is the sum of the roots of 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0?
Simplify √72.
mathematics.explanation: √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2. (Note: 2√18 simplifies further to 6√2, so 6√2 is the fully simplified form.)

mathematics.question: Find the 10th term of the A.P. 3, 7, 11, ...
Find the sum of the first 20 terms of an A.P. with first term 2 and common difference 3.
Find the 4th term of the G.P. 2, 6, 18, ...
What is the value of sin 60°?
Solve for x: x + y = 7 and x − y = 3.
mathematics.explanation: Adding the equations: 2x = 10, so x = 5 (and y = 2).

mathematics.question: If y = x³, find dy/dx.
Differentiate y = 3x² + 2x − 5.
mathematics.explanation: d/dx(3x²) = 6x; d/dx(2x) = 2; the constant vanishes. dy/dx = 6x + 2.

mathematics.question: Find the minimum value of y = x² − 4x + 1.
mathematics.explanation: dy/dx = 2x − 4 = 0 ⇒ x = 2. Then y = 4 − 8 + 1 = −3, the minimum value.

mathematics.question: Evaluate ∫ 6x dx.
Two fair dice are thrown once. What is the probability of obtaining a total score of 7?
Find the mean of the numbers 4, 8, 6, 10 and 7.
Find the median of 3, 7, 4, 9, 5.
Evaluate the determinant of the matrix ⎡2  3⎤ / ⎣1  4⎦.

english.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the capitalised word: The witness gave a CANDID account of the event.
english.explanation: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward; 'frank' is its nearest synonym.

english.question: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the capitalised word: Food was SCARCE during the drought.
english.explanation: The opposite of 'scarce' is 'abundant' - existing in large quantities.

english.question: Neither the boys nor the girl _____ here yesterday.
english.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject - 'the girl' - so it takes 'was'.

english.question: You will come to the party, _____?
english.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag of the same auxiliary: 'will' becomes 'won't you'.

english.question: Choose the correct passive form of: 'The teacher praised the boy.'
options: The boy was praised by the teacher.
The boy was being praised by the teacher.
The boy is praised by the teacher.
The boy had been praised by the teacher.
english.explanation: Simple past active 'praised' becomes simple past passive 'was praised'.

english.question: The doctor advised him to abstain _____ smoking.
english.explanation: The verb 'abstain' is followed by the preposition 'from'.

english.question: 'The duo decided to bury the hatchet' means they decided to _____.
english.explanation: To 'bury the hatchet' is an idiom meaning to end a quarrel and make peace.

english.question: Which of the following words has the same vowel sound as 'food' /uː/?
english.explanation: 'Mood' has the long /uː/ sound of 'food'; 'blood' and 'flood' take /ʌ/, and 'good' takes the short /ʊ/.

english.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the capitalised word: The BENEVOLENT woman donated her fortune to the school.
english.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly disposed; 'kind' is nearest in meaning.

english.question: The news broadcast on television last night _____ very encouraging.
english.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb; 'last night' fixes the tense as past.

english.question: In the sentence, 'The allegation about bribes was a red herring', the paragraph means the allegation was _____.
english.explanation: A 'red herring' is something that diverts attention from the real issue - a distraction.

english.question: Choose the correct reported form: He said, 'I am tired.'
options: He said that he was tired.
He said that he is tired.
He said that I was tired.
He said that he had been tired.
english.explanation: In reported speech the present tense shifts back: 'am' becomes 'was', and 'I' becomes 'he'.

english.question: The carpenter used a _____ to make the surface of the wood smooth.
english.explanation: A plane is the carpenter's tool for smoothing wooden surfaces; a chisel cuts, a mallet strikes.

english.question: 'The argument was as clear as crystal' is an example of _____.
english.explanation: The comparison uses 'as...as', the marker of a simile.

english.question: 'The wind whispered through the trees' illustrates _____.
english.explanation: The wind is given the human quality of whispering - that is personification.

english.question: In 'JOHN bought a car', where the capitalised word is emphasised, the sentence answers the question _____.
english.explanation: Emphatic stress on the subject signals that the question concerns the doer of the action.

english.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the capitalised word: The accountant was METICULOUS in keeping the records.
english.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail - very careful.

english.question: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the capitalised word: His interest in the project was only TRANSIENT.
english.explanation: 'Transient' means lasting only a short time; its opposite is 'permanent'.

english.question: Each and every one of us _____ guilty of the offence.
english.explanation: 'Each and every one' is singular and takes a singular verb - 'is'.

english.question: 'The disgraced official was told to face the music' means he was told to _____.
options: accept the consequences of his actions
english.explanation: To 'face the music' is to accept the unpleasant consequences of one's own actions.

english.question: The meeting was called _____ because of the student's unrest.
english.explanation: To 'call off' a meeting is to cancel it.

english.question: The phrase 'at sixes and sevens' means _____.
english.explanation: To be 'at sixes and sevens' is to be in confusion or disarray.

english.question: The list of candidates _____ of ten names.
english.explanation: 'Consist' is a stative verb (no continuous form) and 'the list' is singular, so 'consists' is correct.

english.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the capitalised word in: 'His FRIVOLOUS remarks annoyed the principal.'
english.explanation: 'Frivolous' means lacking seriousness or sense - 'not serious'.

physics.question: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity?
physics.explanation: Mass, length, time, temperature, electric current, amount of substance and luminous intensity are fundamental; velocity, force and energy are derived.

physics.question: The SI unit of force is the _____.
physics.explanation: Force (mass × acceleration, kg m/s²) is measured in newtons.

physics.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
physics.explanation: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Velocity is directed speed; the others have magnitude only.

physics.question: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 5 s. Its final velocity is _____.
A spring of force constant 100 N/m is stretched by 0.03 m. Calculate the applied force.
physics.explanation: By Hooke's law, F = ke = 100 × 0.03 = 3 N.

physics.question: A block has a mass of 200 g and a volume of 50 cm³. Its density is _____.
physics.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 200/50 = 4 g/cm³.

physics.question: Calculate the kinetic energy of a body of mass 2 kg moving with a velocity of 3 m/s.
physics.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 J.

physics.question: The SI unit of specific heat capacity is _____.
physics.explanation: From Q = mcΔθ, c = Q/(mΔθ), giving joules per kilogram per kelvin: J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

physics.question: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 4 m. Its velocity is _____.
Which of the following is a longitudinal wave?
physics.explanation: In a longitudinal wave the particles vibrate parallel to the direction of travel - the case for sound. Light, ripples and radio waves are transverse.

physics.question: The period of a wave of frequency 25 Hz is _____.
The image formed by a plane mirror is always _____.
physics.explanation: A plane mirror gives a virtual, upright, laterally inverted image the same size as the object.

physics.question: When a ray of light passes from air into water, it bends _____.
physics.explanation: Water is optically denser than air, so the ray slows down and bends towards the normal.

physics.question: A potential difference of 6 V is applied across a 3 Ω resistor. The current flowing is _____.
physics.explanation: By Ohm's law, I = V/R = 6/3 = 2 A.

physics.question: Two resistors of 2 Ω each are connected in parallel. Their effective resistance is _____.
physics.explanation: 1/R = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1, so R = 1 Ω. Equal resistors in parallel: R/n = 2/2 = 1 Ω.

physics.question: The instrument used for measuring electric current is the _____.
physics.explanation: Current is measured with an ammeter connected in series; a voltmeter measures potential difference.

physics.question: According to Newton's law of universal gravitation, the force between two masses is inversely proportional to _____.
options: the square of the distance between them
physics.explanation: F = Gm₁m₂/r² - the force varies inversely with the square of the separation.

physics.question: A capacitor stores a charge of 10 μC when connected across a 5 V battery. Its capacitance is _____.
Fleming's left-hand rule is used to determine the direction of _____.
options: the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
the induced current in a generator
the magnetic field around a wire
physics.explanation: The left-hand (motor) rule gives the direction of the force (motion); the right-hand rule handles induced currents.

physics.question: The photoelectric effect provides evidence that light behaves as _____.
physics.explanation: The emission of electrons depends on frequency, not intensity - evidence that light energy arrives in packets (photons).

physics.question: A radioactive sample of 80 g has a half-life of 4 days. What mass remains after 8 days?
physics.explanation: 8 days = 2 half-lives: 80 → 40 → 20 g.

physics.question: Doping a pure semiconductor with a pentavalent impurity produces _____.
physics.explanation: Pentavalent (donor) atoms add free electrons as majority carriers, giving an n-type material.

chemistry.question: The atomic number of an element is the number of _____ in the nucleus of its atom.
chemistry.explanation: Atomic number Z = number of protons (which equals the number of electrons in a neutral atom).

chemistry.question: Isotopes of the same element differ in the number of _____.
chemistry.explanation: Isotopes have the same proton number but different numbers of neutrons, hence different mass numbers.

chemistry.question: The electronic configuration of sodium (Na, atomic number 11) is _____.
chemistry.explanation: Sodium fills two electrons in the first shell, eight in the second, leaving one valence electron: 2,8,1.

chemistry.question: Elements in Group I of the periodic table are known as _____.
chemistry.explanation: Group I metals (Li, Na, K, ...) are the alkali metals - soft, reactive metals with one valence electron.

chemistry.question: The chemical symbol Fe represents the element _____.
chemistry.explanation: Fe comes from 'ferrum', the Latin name for iron.

chemistry.question: An insoluble solid can best be separated from a liquid by _____.
chemistry.explanation: Filtration traps the insoluble solid (residue) while the liquid passes through (filtrate).

chemistry.question: Common salt is best recovered from its solution in water by _____.
chemistry.explanation: The dissolved salt cannot be filtered; evaporating or crystallizing drives off the water to recover it.

chemistry.question: The most abundant gas in the atmosphere is _____.
chemistry.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air; oxygen is about 21%.

chemistry.question: How many moles are contained in 8 g of methane, CH₄? [C = 12, H = 1]
The number of particles in one mole of a substance is _____.
chemistry.explanation: One mole contains Avogadro's number of particles: 6.02 × 10²³.

chemistry.question: Boyle's law states that at constant temperature, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is _____.
chemistry.explanation: Boyle's law: PV = constant; V ∝ 1/P at constant temperature.

chemistry.question: A gas occupies 2 dm³ at 300 kPa. At constant temperature, what pressure will compress it to 1 dm³?
chemistry.explanation: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ ⇒ P₂ = (300 × 2)/1 = 600 kPa.

chemistry.question: Powdered calcium carbonate reacts faster with dilute hydrochloric acid than the lump form because the powder _____.
chemistry.explanation: Grinding exposes more particles to the acid - a larger contact surface gives more frequent effective collisions.

chemistry.question: The pH of a solution that is 0.001 M hydrochloric acid is _____.
chemistry.explanation: HCl is fully ionized: [H⁺] = 10⁻³ M, so pH = −log(10⁻³) = 3.

chemistry.question: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by _____.
options: providing an alternative path of lower activation energy
shifting the equilibrium to the right
increasing the temperature of the reactants
being used up in the reaction
chemistry.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy and is recovered unchanged at the end of the reaction.

chemistry.question: In an acidic solution, blue litmus paper turns _____.
chemistry.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red; alkalis turn red litmus blue.

chemistry.question: The general molecular formula of the alkanes is _____.
chemistry.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; alkenes follow CₙH₂ₙ.

chemistry.question: The IUPAC name of the compound CH₃CH₂OH is _____.
chemistry.explanation: Two carbons ('ethan-') plus the alkanol '-OH' group ('-ol') give ethanol.

chemistry.question: Successive members of a homologous series differ by _____.
chemistry.explanation: Each member of a homologous series differs from the next by a -CH₂- unit (relative molecular mass of 14).

chemistry.question: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements exhibit _____.
chemistry.explanation: Structural isomerism is the existence of compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures.

chemistry.question: The functional group of the alkanols is _____.
chemistry.explanation: Alkanols (alcohols) contain the hydroxyl group, -OH; -COOH is for alkanoic acids, -CHO for alkanals.

chemistry.question: Ethene undergoes addition polymerization to give _____.
chemistry.explanation: Many ethene monomers join across the double bond to form polyethene (polythene).

chemistry.question: During electrolysis, cations migrate towards the _____.
chemistry.explanation: Cations are positively charged and are attracted to the negative electrode - the cathode.

chemistry.question: In the electrolysis of concentrated brine using inert electrodes, the gas liberated at the cathode is _____.
chemistry.explanation: Hydrogen is discharged at the cathode (lower discharge potential than Na⁺); chlorine is freed at the anode.

chemistry.question: Oxidation is defined as the _____.
chemistry.explanation: OILRIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain of electrons. (Oxidation also includes loss of hydrogen / gain of oxygen.)

chemistry.question: For an exothermic reaction, the enthalpy change ΔH is _____.
chemistry.explanation: Heat is released to the surroundings, so the products have less energy than the reactants and ΔH < 0.

biology.question: The organelle described as the powerhouse of the cell is the _____.
biology.explanation: Cellular respiration occurs in the mitochondria, where energy (ATP) is released.

biology.question: Which of the following structures is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
biology.explanation: Chloroplasts (like cellulose cell walls and large vacuoles) occur only in plant cells.

biology.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of living things?
biology.explanation: Rusting is a chemical change in metals; the standard characteristics are Movement, Respiration, Nutrition, Irritability, Growth, Excretion, Reproduction and Death (MR NIGER D).

biology.question: The binomial system of naming organisms was introduced by _____.
biology.explanation: Linnaeus devised the two-name (genus + species) system of nomenclature.

biology.question: Bacteria are placed in the kingdom _____.
biology.explanation: The five-kingdom scheme puts unicellular prokaryotes - the bacteria - in Monera.

biology.question: A microscope with an eyepiece of ×10 and an objective lens of ×40 gives a total magnification of _____.
biology.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective = 10 × 40 = ×400.

biology.question: The cell theory states that the cell is the basic unit of _____.
options: structure and function of living things
biology.explanation: All living organisms are made of cells, and the cell is the smallest unit capable of carrying out life processes.

biology.question: An example of a unicellular organism is _____.
biology.explanation: Amoeba (like Paramecium and Euglena) is a single-celled protozoan; the others are multicellular.

biology.question: The gas released as a by-product of photosynthesis is _____.
biology.explanation: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ - oxygen is released from the splitting of water.

biology.question: The site of photosynthesis in a green plant cell is the _____.
biology.explanation: Chlorophyll trapped in the chloroplasts absorbs the light energy that drives photosynthesis.

biology.question: The enzyme in saliva that begins the digestion of starch is _____.
biology.explanation: Salivary amylase converts cooked starch to maltose in the mouth.

biology.question: The end products of the digestion of proteins are _____.
biology.explanation: Proteins → polypeptides → amino acids; fatty acids and glycerol come from lipids, glucose from starch.

biology.question: In mammals, oxygen is transported in the blood by the _____.
biology.explanation: Haemoglobin in the red blood cells binds oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin.

biology.question: Water and mineral salts are transported from the roots to the leaves through the _____.
biology.explanation: The xylem carries water and dissolved minerals upward; the phloem translocates manufactured food.

biology.question: Organisms that feed on dead organic matter and return nutrients to the soil are called _____.
biology.explanation: Bacteria and fungi act as decomposers (saprophytes), breaking down dead remains.

biology.question: When two heterozygous tall plants (Tt × Tt) are crossed, the phenotypic ratio of the offspring is _____.
biology.explanation: Genotypes: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt. Since T is dominant, TT and Tt are tall - 3:1 phenotypic ratio.

biology.question: The type of cell division that produces gametes with half the chromosome number is _____.
biology.explanation: Meiosis is reduction division: diploid cells produce haploid gametes; mitosis conserves the chromosome number.

biology.question: The basic unit of inheritance is the _____.
biology.explanation: A gene is a segment of DNA controlling a particular character; chromosomes simply carry many genes.

biology.question: Which of the following is an example of continuous variation in humans?
biology.explanation: Height shows a graded range of values (no distinct classes), unlike blood group which falls into discrete categories.

biology.question: The theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed by _____.
biology.explanation: Darwin (with Wallace) proposed that organisms with favourable variations survive and reproduce - natural selection.

biology.question: The part of the mammalian brain responsible for balance and posture is the _____.
biology.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates muscular movement and maintains balance; the medulla controls involuntary actions.

biology.question: A deficiency of insulin in the body leads to _____.
biology.explanation: Insulin lowers blood glucose; its deficiency leaves blood sugar high - diabetes mellitus.

biology.question: In a reflex action, impulses travel from the receptor to the central nervous system through the _____.
biology.explanation: Reflex arc: receptor → sensory neurone → CNS (relay) → motor neurone → effector.

economics.question: Economics is best defined as the study of how society _____.
options: allocates its scarce resources among competing wants
economics.explanation: The core of economics is scarcity: unlimited wants against limited resources, forcing choice.

economics.question: The opportunity cost of a choice is _____.
options: the money price paid for the item
the total of all alternatives given up
the benefit enjoyed from the choice
economics.explanation: Opportunity cost is the single best alternative sacrificed, not the money spent.

economics.question: The reward for labour as a factor of production is _____.
economics.explanation: Land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest, and the entrepreneur earns profit.

economics.question: A scale of preference is important because it _____.
options: helps an individual rank wants and make rational choices
increases the income of the consumer
economics.explanation: By ranking wants in order of importance, a scale of preference guides choice under scarcity.

economics.question: The fundamental economic problem facing all societies is _____.
economics.explanation: Scarcity forces every economy to answer what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce.

economics.question: Other things being equal, when the price of a commodity rises, the quantity demanded _____.
economics.explanation: The law of demand describes an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded.

economics.question: A market is best described as any arrangement where _____.
options: buyers and sellers are brought into contact to exchange goods and services
fixed prices are set by government
economics.explanation: A market needs buyers, sellers and a means of contact - it may be physical or virtual.

economics.question: Utility in economics means the _____.
options: satisfaction derived from consuming a commodity
usefulness of money in the bank
price of a good in the market
economics.explanation: Utility is the satisfaction a consumer obtains; it is subjective and differs from person to person.

economics.question: Price elasticity of demand is measured as _____.
options: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price
% change in price ÷ % change in quantity demanded
change in price × change in quantity
% change in income ÷ % change in demand
economics.explanation: PED = ΔQd% / ΔP%. Values above 1 are elastic; below 1 are inelastic.

economics.question: A market structure with many buyers and sellers dealing in an identical product is _____.
economics.explanation: Perfect competition has many buyers and sellers, a homogeneous product and no barrier to entry.

economics.question: A market in which there is only one seller of a commodity is called _____.
economics.explanation: A single seller with no close substitutes defines a monopoly.

economics.question: Which of the following is a function of money?
economics.explanation: Money serves as a medium of exchange, a unit of account, a store of value and a standard for deferred payment.

economics.question: Inflation is defined as a persistent rise in the _____.
economics.explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the average (general) level of prices, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

economics.question: The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country is the total value of goods and services produced _____.
options: within the country's borders in a given period
by its citizens abroad in a year
economics.explanation: GDP counts output produced within the geographical boundaries; GNP counts output by nationals wherever they are.

economics.question: The optimum population of a country is the population size that, combined with available resources, yields the _____.
economics.explanation: At optimum population, output per capita is at its highest given existing resources and technology.

economics.question: The Central Bank of Nigeria commenced operations in _____.
economics.explanation: The CBN was established by the 1958 Act and began operations on 1 July 1959 - a classic JAMB fact.

economics.question: The theory of comparative advantage in international trade is associated with _____.
economics.explanation: Ricardo showed countries gain by specialising where their relative (comparative) cost advantage is greatest.

economics.question: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was established in _____.
economics.explanation: ECOWAS was founded by the Lagos Treaty of 28 May 1975 to promote regional economic cooperation.

government.question: The arm of government responsible for implementing laws is the _____.
government.explanation: The executive implements and enforces laws; the legislature makes them and the judiciary interprets them.

government.question: 'Government of the people, by the people and for the people' is the definition of democracy given by _____.
government.explanation: The famous Gettysburg definition of democracy came from American President Abraham Lincoln.

government.question: The primary function of the legislature in a modern state is to _____.
government.explanation: Law-making is the legislature's core function, alongside representation and oversight of the executive.

government.question: A constitution is described as rigid when it _____.
options: cannot be interpreted by the courts
government.explanation: A rigid constitution requires a special, difficult procedure for amendment, unlike a flexible one.

government.question: A classic example of a country operating an unwritten constitution is _____.
government.explanation: Britain's constitution is uncodified - drawn from statutes, conventions and case law.

government.question: A person who owes allegiance to a state and is entitled to its protection is a _____.
government.explanation: Citizenship is the legal bond of allegiance between a person and a state, with reciprocal rights and duties.

government.question: The right of qualified adults to vote in an election is called _____.
government.explanation: Franchise (suffrage) is the right to vote; universal adult suffrage extends it to all qualified adults.

government.question: Indirect rule in Northern Nigeria was introduced by _____.
government.explanation: Lugard administered Northern Nigeria through the emirs - the hallmark of indirect rule.

government.question: The traditional political system of the Igbo of pre-colonial Nigeria is best described as _____.
government.explanation: Igbo villages ruled through councils of elders and age grades, without a single paramount ruler - a segmentary (acephalous) system.

government.question: The first political party in Nigeria, founded in 1923, was the _____.
government.explanation: Herbert Macaulay founded the NNDP in 1923 following the Clifford Constitution of 1922.

government.question: The National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC) was formed in _____.
government.explanation: The NCNC was formed in 1944 with Herbert Macaulay as first president and Nnamdi Azikiwe as secretary.

government.question: Nigeria became a republic in _____.
government.explanation: The 1963 Republican Constitution replaced the Queen with a Nigerian President; Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe became the first President.

government.question: The first indigenous Governor-General of Nigeria was _____.
government.explanation: Azikiwe served as Nigeria's first indigenous Governor-General from 1960 before becoming President in 1963.

government.question: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria introduced the _____.
government.explanation: The 1979 Constitution adopted the American-style executive presidency, replacing the First Republic's Westminster model.

government.question: The federal character principle in Nigeria is designed to _____.
options: ensure fair representation of all states and groups in public appointments
make one region dominate the civil service
government.explanation: Federal character guarantees that ministries, agencies and appointments reflect Nigeria's diversity.

government.question: The first military coup in Nigeria took place in _____.
government.explanation: The coup of 15 January 1966, led by Major Nzeogwu and others, ended the First Republic.

government.question: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) was established in _____.
government.explanation: General Abubakar's transition programme created INEC in 1998 to conduct the 1999 elections.

government.question: The United Nations Organization (UNO) was founded in _____.
government.explanation: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco in June 1945, replacing the League of Nations.

government.question: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) was transformed into the African Union in _____.
government.explanation: The AU was officially launched in Durban, South Africa, in July 2002, succeeding the OAU founded in 1963.

literature.question: The three main genres of literature are _____.
literature.explanation: Literature is conventionally divided into prose, poetry and drama; the other options are sub-forms.

literature.question: A long narrative poem that celebrates the heroic deeds of a legendary figure is _____.
literature.explanation: The epic recounts heroic adventures on a grand scale (e.g. the Epic of Sundiata); a ballad tells shorter folk stories.

literature.question: 'The classroom was a zoo during the break' is an example of _____.
literature.explanation: The classroom is directly called a zoo - a direct comparison without 'like' or 'as' - a metaphor.

literature.question: The repetition of the same initial consonant sound in neighbouring words, as in 'Peter Piper picked...', is called _____.
literature.explanation: Alliteration repeats initial consonant sounds; assonance repeats vowel sounds within words.

literature.question: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem is a _____.
literature.explanation: A stanza is the 'verse paragraph' of a poem, set off by a space; a refrain is a repeated line.

literature.question: A short story in which animals speak and act like humans to teach a moral lesson is _____.
literature.explanation: Fables such as the tortoise tales use animal characters to embody human foibles and end with a moral.

literature.question: 'I have told you a million times to lock the door' illustrates _____.
literature.explanation: 'A million times' is deliberate exaggeration for emphasis - hyperbole.

literature.question: The use of words whose sounds suggest their meaning, such as 'buzz' and 'hiss', is _____.
literature.explanation: Onomatopoeia imitates natural sounds in words.

literature.question: A poem of fourteen lines, usually in iambic pentameter, is _____.
literature.explanation: The sonnet (Petrarchan or Shakespearean) contains exactly fourteen lines.

literature.question: A poem written to mourn the dead is _____.
literature.explanation: An elegy laments a death, whereas an ode addresses or celebrates its subject.

literature.question: A narrator who knows the thoughts and feelings of every character in a story is _____.
literature.explanation: The omniscient ('all-knowing') narrator sees into every character's mind; the first-person narrator is limited to 'I'.

literature.question: A play which ends in the downfall or death of the hero, moving the audience to pity and fear, is _____.
literature.explanation: Tragedy depicts the fall of a noble protagonist; comedy ends happily, often in marriage or reconciliation.

literature.question: When the audience knows more about events than the characters on stage, the effect is called _____.
literature.explanation: Dramatic irony exploits the gap between what the audience knows and what the characters know.

literature.question: A speech in which a character, alone on stage, reveals his inner thoughts to the audience is _____.
literature.explanation: In a soliloquy the character thinks aloud alone; an aside is a brief remark others on stage do not hear.

literature.question: A remark made by a character which is heard by the audience but not by the other characters on stage is _____.
literature.explanation: The aside breaks the dramatic illusion briefly so the audience alone shares a secret.

literature.question: An interruption of a narrative to present events that happened earlier is known as _____.
literature.explanation: Flashback (analepsis) rewinds the story to a past event; foreshadowing hints at what is to come.

literature.question: The overall emotional atmosphere a literary work creates in the reader is its _____.
literature.explanation: Mood is what the reader feels; tone is the writer's attitude towards the subject. The two are frequently confused in exams.

literature.question: The weakness of character which brings about the downfall of a tragic hero is called _____.
literature.explanation: Hamartia is the tragic flaw or error of judgement in Aristotle's account of tragedy.

literature.question: Verse written in unrhymed iambic pentameter is described as _____.
literature.explanation: Blank verse keeps the iambic pentameter rhythm but drops rhyme - the medium of much Shakespearean drama.

literature.question: The unravelling or resolution of the complications of a plot at the end of a play or novel is the _____.
literature.explanation: The denouement unties the knot of the plot after the climax; exposition introduces it.

civic-education.question: Civic education primarily focuses on the _____.
civic-education.explanation: Civic education equips citizens with knowledge of their rights, duties and the workings of government.

civic-education.question: Societal values are best described as the _____.
options: cherished principles and standards that guide behaviour
laws made by the national assembly
civic-education.explanation: Values - honesty, integrity, fairness - are shared standards that shape conduct in a society.

civic-education.question: The virtue of always telling the truth and being fair in dealings with others is _____.
civic-education.explanation: Honesty combines truthfulness with fairness; it attracts trust and responsibility.

civic-education.question: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations in _____.
civic-education.explanation: The UDHR was proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948.

civic-education.question: The rule of law means that _____.
options: everyone is equal before the law and the law is supreme
the president is above the law
civic-education.explanation: Under the rule of law, nobody - including leaders - is above the law, and all are equal before it.

civic-education.question: Free and fair elections, rule of law and an independent judiciary are pillars of _____.
civic-education.explanation: These institutions protect the people's will - the essence of democratic governance.

civic-education.question: Nigeria's official Democracy Day is celebrated every year on _____.
civic-education.explanation: Since 2019, Democracy Day has been observed on June 12 in honour of the annulled 1993 election won by M. K. O. Abiola.

civic-education.question: Which of the following is an example of a fundamental human right?
options: right to vote at any age
civic-education.explanation: The right to life, dignity, personal liberty and fair hearing are fundamental rights in Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution.

civic-education.question: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was established in _____.
civic-education.explanation: The EFCC was set up in 2003 to fight economic and financial crimes such as fraud and money laundering.

civic-education.question: The agency responsible for regulating food and drug standards in Nigeria is _____.
civic-education.explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) guards against fake and substandard products.

civic-education.question: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) was established in _____.
civic-education.explanation: The FRSC was created in 1988 to make Nigerian highways safe and to check road traffic crashes.

civic-education.question: The body charged with fighting the production and trafficking of hard drugs in Nigeria is the _____.
civic-education.explanation: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency targets drug barons and trafficking networks.

civic-education.question: The full meaning of HIV is _____.
civic-education.explanation: HIV - the Human Immunodeficiency Virus - attacks the immune system and can lead to AIDS if untreated.

civic-education.question: HIV can be transmitted through all of the following EXCEPT _____.
civic-education.explanation: HIV is NOT spread by casual contact such as hugging, handshakes or sharing plates.

civic-education.question: The doctrine of separation of powers was popularised by _____.
civic-education.explanation: In 'The Spirit of Laws' (1748), Montesquieu argued that liberty is safest when executive, legislative and judicial powers are held separately.

civic-education.question: The constitution currently in operation in Nigeria is the _____.
civic-education.explanation: Nigeria returned to civil rule on 29 May 1999 under the 1999 Constitution (as amended).

civic-education.question: One important duty of a citizen to the state is _____.
civic-education.explanation: Duties of citizens include paying taxes, obeying laws, voting and defending the nation.

civic-education.question: The green colour in the Nigerian national flag represents _____.
civic-education.explanation: The white band stands for peace; the two green bands represent agriculture and the country's natural wealth.
